messages.content: You are a precise information extraction system. You only output valid JSON.

Extract all entity mentions from the document.

Entity types:
- Person: a named or described human individual or group of people
- Organization: a company, army, government body, team, party or other organised group
- Location: a geographic place: country, city, region, body of water, battlefield, etc.
- Building: a man-made structure or facility: hotel, fort, bridge, airport, etc.
- Product: a man-made object or product: vehicle, ship, aircraft, weapon model, etc.
- Art: a creative work: book, film, song, painting, etc.
- Other: any other named thing relevant to events (e.g. nationalities, named events, ideologies)

Entity annotation rules:
- Annotate named entities AND other mentions that refer to them: nominal phrases ("the plane", "the storm"), subject/object pronouns ("he", "she", "they", "him"), and nationality/group words ("British", "Ottomans").
- Do NOT annotate possessive pronouns ("his", "her", "their", "its"), dates or years ("3 January 1992", "2013").
- Numbers, quantities, ordinals and durations ("13", "two", "3rd", "two days") are entities of type Other.
- Annotate every occurrence, including repeated mentions of the same entity.
- Nationality or group words are typed by what they refer to: a country/place -> Location, an army/state/organisation -> Organization, a people -> Person.

Return JSON: {"entities": [{"text": "<mention copied from the document>", "type": "<entity type>"}]}

### Now the target
Document:
The 1924 Cuba hurricane is the earliest officially classified Category 5 Atlantic hurricane on the Saffir–Simpson scale (SSHS), and one of two hurricanes to make landfall on Cuba at Category 5 intensity, the other being Hurricane Irma in 2017 – both are also tied for the strongest Cuban landfall in terms of maximum sustained winds. The hurricane formed on October 14 in the western Caribbean, slowly organizing as it tracked northwestward. By October 16, the storm attained hurricane status to the east of the Yucatán Peninsula, and subsequently executed a small counterclockwise loop. On October 18, the hurricane began undergoing rapid deepening and, on the next day, reached an estimated peak intensity of 165 mph (270 km/h). Shortly thereafter, it struck extreme western Cuba at peak intensity, becoming the strongest hurricane on record to hit the country. Later the hurricane weakened greatly, striking southwestern Florida with winds of 90 mph (150 km/h) in a sparsely populated region. While crossing the state it weakened to tropical storm status, and after accelerating east-northeastward, it was absorbed by a cold front on October 23, to the south of Bermuda. Across the western Caribbean Sea, the developing storm produced heavy rainfall and increased winds. Strong winds in western Cuba caused severe damage, with two small towns nearly destroyed. About 90 people were killed in the country, all in Pinar del Río Province. Later, the hurricane brought heavy rainfall to southern Florida, which caused flooding and crop damage. Damage was light in the state, and there were no casualties.
